title: Playback Runtime Resource Scheduler
problem: Playback runtime resource limits exist in several places, but Nako lacks one host-owned admission boundary for direct, remux, HLS, remote stream, and future transcode workloads.

evidence.summary: Opened the durable playback runtime resource scheduler lane, linked it from playback architecture indexes, and froze single-node admission as the first proof before remote workers, queueing, LL-HLS, DASH, or DRM.

Added a server-owned playback resource demand and admission decision model for direct streams, remux, and HLS. The model explains accepted, rejected, and not-yet-enforced classes while preserving current route behavior.
Enforced admission permits for HLS and remux process-backed start paths, including browser playback preflight starts, while keeping existing session reuse permit-free.
Surfaced redaction-safe playback resource pressure in Admin runtime diagnostics and refreshed Admin TypeScript contracts.

Verified and documented closeout, updated playback architecture indexes, and split queueing, remote workers, OS isolation, per-device tuning, LL-HLS/DASH, DRM, and HLS artifact I/O enforcement into follow-ons.

continue_policy.notes: The single-node playback runtime resource scheduler first slice is complete. Open new follow-on workstreams for admission queueing, remote transcode workers, OS resource isolation, per-device capacity tuning, LL-HLS/DASH, DRM/key delivery, or HLS artifact I/O pressure enforcement.
